newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech MST undervalued, but a hold - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech MST undervalued, but a hold - analysts.

text.p: Shares of the eastern Czech heat utility Moravskoslezske Teplarny (MST) are undervalued at 950 crowns each, but the stock is a hold until the effects of ownership changes are clear, analysts said.
"Results of heat companies for the last year and for this year will be positively influenced by the long and cold winter," Leos Jirman, an analyst at Delta Securities said.

After Prague utility Prazska Teplarenska a.s., MST is the second largest district heat producer and distributor in the Czech Republic. Heat sales, especially to large communist-era housing estates, create three quarters of the company's income.
"On the other hand, results of such companies would also be influenced by still regulated heat prices," Jirman said.
Shares of MST gained three crowns on Monday to 950. At this price the profit earnings ratio is 6.4 which Romana Juras from Brno Broker Group said was fundamentally low.
In the first three quarters of 1996, MST sales rose by 15 percent year-on-year and profit was up 9.3 percent, helped by good first quarter results and the long winter.
Ivo Pestuka from Atlantik Financial markets says in the fourth quarter of the year the profit's growth should continue as the period traditionally is profitable for heat companies.
"This is the reason why we see (net) profit of MST around 421 million crowns," Pestuka said.
Recently there has been a series of ventures joining Czech heat utilities and local electrical power distributors.

But at the end of the last year a majority stake of the company was bought by its major fuel supplier, coal mining company OKD a.s., and a local company Prosper Trading (of which OKD got 34, and Prosper Trading 17 percent).

Michal Kusak from AKRO Capital says that this acquisition would cut MST's profits, as over one million tonnes of coal from OKD's 13-million tonne production would now go to MST, as OKD plans price increases.

"OKD will in the future direct the purchasing policy of MST. Because OKD, unlike its Polish competitiors, plans price increse, it would have negative impact on (MST's) profits. Shareholders are not likely to see dividend," Kusak said.
But Eric Volkman from Raiffeisen Capital & Investment says the utility's activities would not be influenced by OKD.
"We believe OKD would not change basic business plan of its new acquisition which is absolutely reasonable, well directed and realistic," Volkman said.
MST did not pay a dividend from its 1995 profit, but plans to pay a gross dividend of 35 corwns on 1996 profit rising to 50 crowns by 1998
In 1995, MST posted turnover of 3.4 billion crowns and net profit of 372 million crowns, but profits are expected to trend the other way due to the company's demanding investment plans.
In the next five years the company plans to invest about 6.7 billion crowns mainly into the production of electrical power and into environment friendly measures on its equipment.
More than 50 percent of the investment should be covered from MST's own sources, but loan indebtedness would rise too.
